Hadassah: Easy going? Suuuuuuure, he is! Seemingly fun and irreverent on the surface, Hadassah is incredibly competitive. Is he narrow-minded? Well, we hope not. If he's born in the Middle East he might need to take a chill-pill once in a while, but generally he's okay. (Good friends with Aaron.)
Hadrian: By the time people figure out how his name is spelled Hadrian has come right around and sorted out his shit. So, in life, Hadrian will stick to the programme for longer than you think and almost certainly for longer than you'd hope. No, he's not a boring bastard, but he won't leap of cliff in the nude, first. Girls meet him and presume he is either important or cashed up, and we can tell you he has that potential, if that's your thing, but we suggest he lives with his shoes off for as long as he can. It'll do him good.
Haggis: The absurd and hilarious Scotsman who, while a long way from home, is at home everywhere he goes.
Haim: Haim in never home which worries his parents constantly, although they are well aware that his life decisions are reasonable and well thought out.
Hal: Hal rhymes with Have As Much Fun As Is Reasonably Possible, it rhymes with Think About What You Want and it rhymes with Understand The Consequences Of Your Actions. In short, Hal is a wonderful old sage whose presence opens people up.
Hallam: Hallam is tired of being called Helen, which happens if he stays at the pub late on a Friday night. At least, it used to happen until he decided to stop going. Having said all that, he does like snake skin boots so who knows, maybe there is a hidden Helen in there after all?
Hamish: A reliable and kind-hearted fellow who doesn’t beat around the bush despite being raised there. “Are you talking to me?” he asks with complete sincerity. “What do you want?”
Hank: The name of the filthy fat man who is driving the tow-truck that comes to rescue you in a dodgy part of town at 3 o’clock in the morning. You can smell his body odour before he gets out of the truck, which in itself is also bad for the environment, and he is one of the most splendid visions you have ever seen in your life.
Hanlon:
It's 3 o'clock in the morning and the mud-crabbing trip has gotten off to an inauspicious start. For the last two hours we've been progressively bogged five different times in a tropical swamp. No one is in peril as there's plenty of beer - we didn't bring any water with us, fuck that - and the crocs are rarely seen this far inland so nobody is going to get eaten. We hope. Just as it seemed we'd cleared the bad bit, however, we've hit one more swampy patch that has gotten us bogged again. “Fucken hell!” everyone curses, just about fed up. Ahead of the troopy we can see that the ground is higher and drier, we think, and just as with everything in life, it seems, here again is one final hurdle we have to jump over before we hit pay-dirt. At this pivotal moment, covered in mud and cold as buggery, the right blend of 'Hanlon' within the group is critical (i.e: the right blend of nous, determination and humour).
If we've got it, we'll get through, have a laugh, drink some piss, catch some muddies' and have a fat time. If we haven’t got any then we're fucked and we're in for a cunt of a night.
Hanno: Hanno never dies wondering. And if he fails, well at least he had a go and stuff the consequences! If we could bottle him and feed him to the nation we might bloody-well change the fate of the planet. Who knows? (Yes, he's ungainly on the dance floor but he can handle a rifle.)
Hans: Like all northern European men Hans laughs at the weirdest things. Never unfriendly and always extremely well-travelled and intelligent, Hans has come to understand what he wants from life and how he wants to live. Rules have never impacted him and he is an independent thinker. Is he a sexual deviant? Mmm, well, we can't say that he is but, equally, we can say he’s more than comfortable being nude in a public place.
Hardie: Hardie drives a Range Rover and he isn't one of these people who never uses its off-road capacity. He enjoys quality in both the people that he mingles with and what he surrounds himself with in life. Well-travelled and well-fed, when he gets there, Hardie will be a cheerful old man who looks a lot more serious than he is. He smokes a pipe and he gets in trouble for flirting with the nurses.
Hardy: Hardy never seeks the spotlight. He’s far more concerned with doing the right thing by the planet, by his kids and by the community at large. As a young man he was damn-near reckless in his various pursuits.
Haren: Haren is a wonderful and quirky little fellow who fossicks about with some kind of constant smile on his face, like he is about to engage in something so ridiculously fun and childishly stupid that he can barely contain himself.
Hari: Hari's house is like a little slice of India. It's full of incence smoke, strange Hindi hangings on the wall, loud twanging Indian music and, while I'm not certain of course, I think that basket in the corner contains a living cobra.
Haris: Succinct in dealings and emotionless to those who don’t know him, Haris exists as a reminder that nothing in life is straightforward.
Harl: Now here is an understated, cool cat. No, Harl isn't shy, he just likes to sit back for a while and take it all in, analyse what's going on around him, let the cafuffle die down before he speaks his piece or makes his move. If you tell Harl a joke and you've just met him, he'll look you in the eye and listen to what you're saying, but all the while at the back of his mind he is endeavouring to look into your soul so see who you really are. To be honest, it's quite a gift. He's no street-sweeper.
Harlan: Outlandish? Nay. Friendly? Yay. Boring? Nay. Lonely? Fucking never.
Harley: Harley is light on his feet and he’d make an excellent thief, rapper or kick-boxer.
Harold: Harold wears full pyjamas to bed every night and tries to sit very straight whenever he eats. It’s good for the digestive system.
Harpur: Is he the most unpanic-ridden person in the Kingdom? Wholly present and relevant, Harpur operates like the Belgian government during their early 'negotiations' with the Nazis.They remained calm, they never got flustered at the increasingly absurd, cruel and unfair restrictions placed upon its Jewish population, and they simply refused to buy into the anger and confusion the Nazis so wished to incite. Now, what does all this mean? Here in the real world Harpur is calm, he carries a peaceful smile everywhere he goes and behind it is the knowledge that every second is worth celebrating. Too right.
Harrison: You poor bugger…..your mother was so enamoured with the Star War’s and Indiana Jones’ character that you’re now carrying the mantle. As a walking cliché I suggest you change your name and give yourself a break. You’re a nice bloke, so what about Bill? Have you thought about that?
Harry: Jocular. He’s never a psychopath and he’s rarely offensive.
Hartmut: Germans, by and large, don't really understand fart jokes. It's lucky then that Hartmut thinks a lot of his German colleagues are a little bit too organised and dull.
Hartwell: If Hartwell were a dog, the only reason he’d ever need a muzzle is because his modus operandi would be to lick everyone to death immediately and constantly. Has he got a wife or a lover of sorts?….Anyone? We should probably talk to them.
Harvey: A well maintained, sufficiently lubricated and perfectly functioning gearbox of a Kenworth truck. He works when he needs to work and he laughs loudly when he wants to laugh loudly. Why wouldn’t you.
Haset: Haset is so full of family love that he is almost exploding. Beyond that, picture a lady called Dot trapped in a male body.
Hass:
If Hass is on a big ship that hits something and sinks, no way will his name appear in the lost at sea ledger, afterwards. We can’t tell you if he’d be heroic or not - we’d like to think that he would do his best to help others in need - but no way is this boy going to drown. 
And he’s probably not going to marry in a hurry either.
Hayden: Well, no, he's not the most skilled player in the group but he trains hard and he's always one of the last to walk into the sheds after a session. In that regard he's quite aware of his skills and his place in the team. On game day he gets his fair share of the ball but it's his attitude and level of endeavour that are his real assets. And make no mistake, the marketing girls always want him in the team photo afterwards, and so long as they're kept happy we'll keep him on the list.
Hayes: Hayes hangs out with the dodgy crew. His earns his dollars via dubious means and while he’s funny enough and pleasant in company, we wouldn’t recommend you loan him any money.
Hazen: Generally modified to be chilled out and affable, Hazen is the sort of fellow who will go out of his way to put in a kind word for a friend in need.
Heath: Unpredictable. You don’t want to meet Heath in a dark alley in a rage.
Heber: Like a head umpire at the final of a Grand Slam event, Heber views the world with a quiet, almost dispassionate expression. He's all ears and eyes, however, and not much gets passed him. And, as ever, he's prepared to deal with an irate player, a problematic injury time as well as heckling from the crowd. He has a low resting pulse.
Hector: It’s 5am at the party, Hector is drunk, he’s tired, and most of all he’s sick of listening to the shit being spoken around him. He stands up from the couch, salutes a fare-ye-well to the remaining rabble before eloquently dodging their friendly abuse and making for the exit. There, in the doorway, freshly entered, is a woman so starkly beautiful Hector is suddenly confounded at how he’d been living without her. Suddenly wide awake, he walks tall towards her and stops in front of her. “Good evening,” he says with a gentle smile. “May I ask your name?”…
Hellfred:
Hellfred's greatest joy in life, aside from driving his polished, red, immaculate MG convertible, generally, is studying his reflection on a bright sunny day, of he himself driving his polished, red, immaculate MG convertible in the shop windows as he motors up the main street. Mirror sunnies on. Slick smirk. Crisp white polo shirt, collar up.

And while many might consider him to be a conceited twit, Hellfred will tell you the whole thing is one giant fucking game, so why not just ham it up? Christ knows someone has to....
Helmut: Tell us he’s a German engineer, surely? Nice fellow, however, but yeah, he’s a German engineer who probably doesn’t fully grasp slapstick comedy.
Hendo: A country boy raised on hard-working country values. Well, that is until he gets on his motorbike and then he's a bloody menace to both himself and everyone else he shares the road with.
Henk: Henk is too brutally honest for either the political or corporate world, and let’s face it, his visage is one only a mother could love, but the truth he speaks is delivered in such a way as to make it one of the funniest things you will ever encounter. Henk ain’t fucking normal, and that’s just the way the good Lord intended it. Amen
Henning: What is it with Danes? He spends most of his time in the nude, even when he's fishing, he is a loving husband and he is a highly experimental cook.
Henri: As something of an eccentric it is a given that Henri possesses a huge intelligence. So what if he wears a bright yellow tuxedo to the awards dinner being given in his honour? What matters most is that Henri is The Crazy Inventor, and we’ll need his help, no matter what he’s wearing.....!
Henry: “Good old Henry,” you say. He’s not bright enough to be evil but he’s certainly good enough to be wonderful. And by God, he is.
Henty: Raised up on a sheep farm, Henty is blessed with giant hands and one of those rural demeanours that makes you feel both calm and safe at the same time. Not to be messed with.
Herb: Herb is the sort of bloke that walks back into the farmhouse at the end of another stiflingly hot day, having spent most of it shooting the sheep on his property that were starving to death in lieu of the drought that has devastated his land and his livelihood, and still has a smile for his wife and kids.
Herbie: Herbie's smile is just a little bit creepy and he pulls his trousers up way too far.
Hercules: As an ex-God he’s allowed a few liberties and he takes them, which is fair enough, but no one ought to get used to resting on their laurels. Doors don’t just magically open these days, chief.
Herman: The Beetle. You know the one. He comes hurtling in the open window like he's flying into battle, crashing with a loud thwack into the curtain. (So much for being discrete!) After he lands you can see him thinking, "Where the fuck am I? What the bloody hell is this place?" And off he goes again, circling around and around looking purposeful, hoping like Christ he can figure out how to get of here before he gets eaten or shot at. Herman.
Hermes: After the bad cop has ranted and raved at the prisoner in the interrogation room with no success, he departs and after a short time, Hermes, the slippery good cop comes into the room. His mood is calm, he even smiles a bit, and he tries to entice the prisoner with encouraging words and the prospect of some kind of deal that might be able to be brokered, so long as the prisoner comes clean. Hermes.
Hernando:
Like an over-horny gorilla who rushes at rivals in the hope he’ll scare them away, Hernando is all bluff and bluster. He hasn’t got a scar on him. He’s a funny guy though. His life mantra?
Have melodrama, will travel.
Herrick: No, he's not Yorrick and no he’s no heretic either, probably. What he is, is humorous, kind and artistic. He get’s bored at the drop of a hat.
Heston: A friendly fellow who dresses well, is courteous to strangers and who is never afraid to wear his heart on his sleeve. If there is a joke to be had, he’ll do his best to include those around him, rather than exclude.
Hilton: Hilton doesn't go in for old rustic homes. What he wants to see is the yard taken over completely by a McMansion that resembles a fortress, and that, in his eyes, consitutes the very latest in modern living. (On the proviso that energy-saving techniques like recycled waste water, a vegetable garden and the like are none of his business. If you can attach a remote control to it or order it on line, including the vegies, then all the better.)
Hinze: Born in Hamburg, Germany, Hinze is now 62 years old and is the chief curator at a rock museum.
Hitch:
Can you imagine Hitch being captured as a POW and brought into the enemy commanders HQ? The first thing he'd do would be to loudly and forcefully describe his superior moral position before insisting the 10 armed men surrounding him lay down their weapons and immediately surrender.

"That's more bloody like it," he'd say. "Now, where do you keep your liquor?"

Hitch
Hoang: The little boy racer with a ton of style.
Hock: Hock spends most of his time looking at the palms of his hands, close up, trying to figure out how his body came to be constructed of star dust. “I mean, how did that happen??....,” he’ll whisper to himself, perplexed.
Hocko: Hocko is the sort of bloke who gets so out of it, one night, he accidentally performs deeds so ridiculous that, not only can we not actually discuss them here, they become folklore. Not that he actually inflicts any kind of pain on anyone, it’s just that, once he gets rolling, Hocko doesn’t possess an off switch. Indeed, the only off switch we’ve ever known to work on him is the brick wall that he ends up crashing into all on his own. Some people just never grow up, do they?
Hogan: No, he's no hero but he does have a large group of friends and an extended family set-up. Property and money are things he seems to deal with well, and it affords him plenty of leisure time. We’re not sure he always uses it wisely, but who are we to suggest any alterations to anyone’s state of happiness, let along Hogan’s.
Holger: A serious Eastern European man who likes his rubber boots, his furry cows and his quite weird pornography collection which defies description here.
Hollywood: Hollywood loves to flaunt it and people are sick of telling him to put it away.
Holt: Holt doesn't wait for anyone to catch up. If he spies an opening and you're late then forget it, because like water he'll slip through the crack and be gone. It’s why he’s a good basket baller even though he’s short.
Horatio:
Horatio is great at being second in charge and no one really takes him too seriously, which is a pity. 
Advice from Management: Fuck it Horatio, get big. In fact, don’t get big, get massive. Embrace the melodrama that people expect of you and be ridiculous, the more the better. We want to see you fly, boy! 
Why the hell not? Good luck.
Howard:
Howard is a saturated log that’s lying on the bottom of a river, or maybe a lake.
 Question:  What’s he doing?
 Answer: Not much.
Howell: Every unexpected event in life presents Howell with an opportunity for philosophical contemplation and humoristic endeavour.
Hoy: Hoy owns a van and for a price he’ll pick-up and remove just about anything at a moments notice. He charges quite a bit more for body disposal you understand, but this is probably fair enough. He doesn’t care what he’s wearing so long as he’s comfortable.
Hubert: As a consequence of a very conservative upbringing he has solid and commendable values that stretch toward intolerance. He cleans out his ears, daily.
Huck: In one of those rare events that even the greatest minds that delve into the complicated mathematics of quantum mechanics are at a loss to define or understand, Huck radiates positive ions. So, take a big breath, stand forth, and just walk into him.
Huddo: More than 150 people have auditioned for the role and still, after three days the producers are sitting in the front row, scratching their heads. But their luck is about to change. Huddo has made a late entrance, as usual, but here we go kids. Broadway will never be the same again. The rest, as they say, is history…
Huddy: An award winning choreographer, set designer, actor, artist or writer.
Hudson: Hudson is handsome (kind of) and funny (sort of), but he is a brooding egomaniac who eventually gives everyone the shits. What is it with these American names?
Huey:
A bumbling good guy who never rushes anything, which is fine. What you may not be aware of however is that Huey, the god, is who every surfer prays to when they're out the back and in need of a wave. You’ll hear someone next to you say aloud in frustration, “Come on Heuy, what are you doin’ mate?”
And you’ll sit there and sure enough, suddenly the horizon changes colour and rises up. Huey was there all the time, you understand. He’s tapped into the Planet Gods because he is one. All we can do is pray he’s on our side. Best bit is, even if you drown, he’s leading you by the hand to the next place. There is nothing he won’t do for you.
Hugh: The Hoarder. Whether he’s an opal prospector, a sculptor of marble or a painter of oil on canvas, Hugh is some kind of artist and he hasn’t showered or shaved in years. (Unless he’s the Hugh that works on the floor of the stock market, in which case I wouldn’t bother with him.)
Hugo: When King Hugo (the full moon) comes out to play, it’s he who casts the spell which makes everyone go crazy – and he brings with him one of the great senses of humour. In human form Hugo is the unofficial leader, though he hates ever being called that, and not just anyone can pull it off. Nice one Hugo.
Humphrey: Humphrey isn’t so much as bold as he is experimental. A rollicking sense of optimism means he is rarely miserable although his mother and partners are perpetually exasperated at how messy he is around the house. He’d make a useless spy because it’s nigh’ impossible for him to leave a scene/cupboard/fridge without leaving evidence of his visit, and in love he is a doting, blithering buffoon, god bless him.
Huon: Educated and relaxed, Huon takes his time and rarely gets flustered.
Hutchy: The Great Egyptian Sphinx. No one knows what he’s thinking although it’s probably pretty good because Hutchy is nothing if not cunning.
Huw: How can you take a man seriously when he doesn't? Perhaps this is why he is so lucky. In essence, Huw doesn't often sit idle and he is huge fun as a result. Good with kids, helpful with neighbours, and he'll try anything once.
Huxton:
He's a freak. No, he's never gone exploring but he loves the idea, however. Inevitably his romantic partners ditch him because they tire of being asked how he looks in, what he calls, his ‘frontier stance’. He places one leg up on the bed, one on the ground, puts his hands on hips and stares off into space as if he were observing a vast untouched mountain range that he’s about to conquer.
Huxton, mate, have you considered getting into the space program? The only place a human is going to be able to do that meaningfully, in the current era, is when we land on Mars, but that's not going to be for a while.
